html:
The ruins of a town of the Tairona people in the mountains of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in northern Colombia, thought to have been founded around 800 CE. Its Spanish name means "lost city"; its local name is Teyuna.

The town is a set of more than 150 round stone terraces cut into a steep forested ridge. Houses of wood and thatch stood on them, linked by stone paths and stairways, with channels to carry off the heavy rain. It was a centre of a network of Tairona towns that traded goods between the coast and the mountains. The Tairona were also skilled goldsmiths.

The site was abandoned during the Spanish conquest in the 1500s. Grave robbers found it again in the early 1970s, and archaeologists followed. The Kogi, Arhuaco and Wiwa, descendants of the Tairona, still live in the Sierra and treat it as sacred. It is older than Machu Picchu by several centuries.
sum: The ruins of a town of the Tairona people in the mountains of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in northern Colombia, thought to have been founded around 800 CE. Its Spanish name means "lost city"; its local name is Teyuna.
